summary: One-day EX751 study plan built and delivered — same format as CT653 reference, weighted by sample-paper repeat frequency + the 4 newly-sourced gap topics, fit into today's 10:00-22:00 + tomorrow's 05:00-09:00 window with sleep excluded.
result_text:
Study plan built: ex751_1day_plan_1000start.html, delivered to user.

Structure — matches CT653 reference file format exactly (dark theme, sticky progress header, checkbox JS, same CSS var scheme), extended with a REPEAT tag for sample-paper-frequency-flagged items.

Priority data pulled via nlm query against sample papers + Final assessment topics.txt (source 0a509b56 + 4fec49d0) before building — topics ranked by repeat count across separate exam papers, categorized numerical/derivation/short-answer/diagram.

Time allocation (10:00 today → 09:00 tomorrow, sleep 22:00-05:00 excluded from content):
- 10:00-22:00 (12h, 8 content blocks + meals/breaks): full first pass, Ch2→Ch3→Ch5→Ch7 in that order, front-loading each chapter's highest-repeat items first, gap-fill topics slotted right after each chapter's core content (not bolted onto the end)
- 05:00-08:15 (3.25h AM): no new content — numerical redo-from-scratch drill, REPEAT-only short-answer speed pass, then a dedicated cold-check block for exactly the 4 newly-sourced gap topics
- 08:15-09:00: buffer + final settle, zero content

25 REPEAT-tagged items (topics hitting 2+ separate sample papers), 10 items covering the 4 newly-sourced gaps (each gets one study-depth slot in the main pass + one cold-check slot in the AM pass, since they have zero repeat history to lean on).

Verified via bash: item/tag counts match design (25 REPEAT, 10 NEW, 13 content blocks) before delivery.
